findings.title: Migration interpolates host values into SQL
findings.body: Line 25 builds INSERT with VALUES ('#{h}', ...) where h comes from the site_settings.embeddable_hosts value. A host containing a single quote breaks the statement or allows SQL injection. The migration will fail or corrupt data on such input. Use connection.quote / sanitize instead of string interpolation.

findings.title: Migration crashes when embed settings are absent
findings.body: Lines 9-16 do execute(...)[0]['id'] and [0]['value'] without checking for empty results. On a fresh install or when embed_category / uncategorized_category_id / embeddable_hosts rows are missing, [0] is nil and nil['id'] raises NoMethodError, failing the whole migration and blocking deploy. Guard for empty results and defaults.

findings.title: Update/destroy crash on unknown id instead of 404
findings.body: Update does EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first then save_host(host) which does host.host=, and destroy does host.destroy. If the id does not exist, host is nil and both actions raise NoMethodError resulting in a 500 instead of 404. Add not-found handling.

findings.title: before_validation crashes on nil host
findings.body: The callback calls self.host.sub! twice without guarding nil. Creating/updating with missing or nil host (e.g. blank form submit via Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host) raises NoMethodError before validation runs, turning a validation error into a 500. Guard with return if host.blank? or use to_s.

findings.title: Host lookup is not case-insensitive despite lower()
findings.body: record_for_host does where("lower(host) = ?", host) where host is uri.host without downcasing. Comparing lower(column) to a mixed-case value like Example.COM never matches, so EmbeddableHost.host_allowed? incorrectly returns false and valid embeds/referers are rejected. Downcase the parameter or compare lower(host)=lower(?).

findings.title: Stored host with port can never match lookup
findings.body: before_validation strips scheme and path but keeps :port, and the format validation allows (:port), so example.com:3000 can be saved. record_for_host uses URI(host).host which strips the port, then compares to the stored value including port, so such a record never matches and EmbedController/TopicRetriever always deny it. Either strip/normalize ports on save or include them in lookup, or disallow ports.

findings.title: No uniqueness validation on host
findings.body: EmbeddableHost only validates format, not uniqueness. Admins can create duplicate host rows with different categories. record_for_host then picks an arbitrary first row, making category assignment and allow-list ambiguous. Add case-insensitive uniqueness validation and a unique DB index.

findings.title: Plural _ids hydration crashes on null
findings.body: The new plural branch does obj[k].map(...) without checking that obj[k] is an array. If the server sends null or undefined for an *_ids field, this throws TypeError and breaks store.find/findAll hydration for that model, including the new embedding payload. Guard for null and filter missing lookups.

findings.title: No coverage for new embedding admin endpoints
findings.body: Both new controller specs only assert subclass of AdminController. There are no tests for create/update/destroy validation, blank host, unknown id 404, auth, or EmbeddingController#show. The nil-deref and validation bugs above are therefore undetected. Add request specs for success and error paths.

findings.title: Fabricator file contents are swapped
findings.body: spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb now defines Fabricator(:embeddable_host) and spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb defines Fabricator(:category) and related categories. The definitions are in the wrong files. It works only because all fabricators are loaded globally, but it is confusing and fragile. Swap the contents back so each file defines its namesake.
